question.text: According to the PFUTP Regulations, which of the following constitutes an unfair trade practice?

answer.text: Executing trades based on publicly available research reports
Short selling with proper disclosure to the exchange
Placing limit orders below the last traded price
A market participant entering into transactions on behalf of a client without the knowledge of or instructions from the client

explanation.text: The Logic: The PFUTP Regulations list, among the unfair trade practices, a market participant entering into transactions on behalf of a client without the knowledge of or instructions from such client, or misutilising or diverting client funds or securities held in a fiduciary capacity. The Trap: Option A (research-based trading), option B (short selling with proper disclosure), and option C (limit orders below LTP) are legitimate trading activities and are not, by themselves, unfair trade practices under the regulation. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-III-A workbook (Dec 2025), page 146, which expressly lists transactions on behalf of a client without the client's knowledge or instructions as an unfair trade practice.
